title: Inverse image along an isomorphism of schemes commutes with tensor products and sheaf Hom
statement:
Let $g:X\to Y$ be an isomorphism of schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], with small pro-etale sites $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$, $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and inverse image $g^{-1}$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Let $\mathcal O$ be a sheaf of commutative rings on $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$, so that $g^{-1}\mathcal O$ is a sheaf of commutative rings on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and $g^{-1}$ carries sheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules to sheaves of $g^{-1}\mathcal O$-modules, and let $\mathcal F,\mathcal G,\mathcal H$ be sheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules. Then there are isomorphisms of sheaves of $g^{-1}\mathcal O$-modules

$$
 \sigma_{\mathcal F,\mathcal G}:g^{-1}(\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal G)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }g^{-1}\mathcal F\otimes_{g^{-1}\mathcal O}g^{-1}\mathcal G,
 \qquad
 \eta_{\mathcal F,\mathcal G}:g^{-1}\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\mathcal Hom_{g^{-1}\mathcal O}(g^{-1}\mathcal F,g^{-1}\mathcal G),
$$

with the tensor product and sheaf Hom of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and [def-pur-sheaf-hom], natural in $\mathcal F$ and $\mathcal G$, such that: $\sigma$ sends $g^{-1}(s\otimes t)$ to $g^{-1}s\otimes g^{-1}t$ and $\eta$ sends $g^{-1}\varphi$ to $g^{-1}(\varphi)$ on local sections; $\sigma$ is compatible with the associativity and commutativity isomorphisms of the tensor product and with the unit isomorphisms $\mathcal O\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal F\cong\mathcal F$, so that it induces isomorphisms $g^{-1}(\mathcal F^{\otimes_{\mathcal O}m})\cong(g^{-1}\mathcal F)^{\otimes_{g^{-1}\mathcal O}m}$ for every $m\geq1$; and for a morphism of sheaves of rings $\mathcal O\to\mathcal O'$ and an $\mathcal O$-module $\mathcal F$, $\sigma$ gives $g^{-1}(\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal O')\cong g^{-1}\mathcal F\otimes_{g^{-1}\mathcal O}g^{-1}\mathcal O'$. The same holds for inverse limits: for an inverse system $(\mathcal F_n)_n$ of $\mathcal O$-modules, $g^{-1}\varprojlim_n\mathcal F_n\cong\varprojlim_ng^{-1}\mathcal F_n$ as $g^{-1}\mathcal O$-modules [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit].

proof.text: Put $\mathcal C=X_{\mathrm{proet}}$, $\mathcal D=Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$. Apply [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image], part 1: $\Phi:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$, $(U,u)\mapsto(U,gu)$, and $\Psi:(V,v)\mapsto(V,g^{-1}v)$ are inverse site equivalences, and $g^{-1}F$ is naturally identified with $TF:=F\circ\Phi^{op}$. Write $SQ=Q\circ\Psi^{op}$. Both reindexings preserve sheaves since they and their inverses preserve coverings. Set $R=T\mathcal O$. For a module sheaf the action on $TF(U)=F(\Phi U)$ is precisely the $\mathcal O(\Phi U)=R(U)$-action. The same relabelling on morphisms has inverse $S$, using the unit and counit of the site equivalence to identify $SR$ with $\mathcal O$. Thus $T$ and $S$ are inverse equivalences on module sheaves and also on module presheaves; linearity and the restriction law are the sectionwise conditions of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. This argument allows an arbitrary sheaf $\mathcal O$ of commutative rings, not just a constant sheaf.

source.place: Tag 03CV (section-sheaves-modules), Definition 03CW (definition-sheaf-modules); site equivalence and section formula: proetale.tex Tag 09A5 (section-morphism), specialized by the cited lemma

proof.text:
For a presheaf $P$ of $\mathcal O$-modules the reindexed sheafification map $TP\to T(P^\#)$ exhibits $T(P^\#)$ as the sheafification of $TP$. Indeed, for any $R$-module sheaf $Q$, reindexing a linear map by $S$, applying the universal property in [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], and reindexing back give mutually inverse bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}(TP,Q)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(P,SQ)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(P^\#,SQ)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(T(P^\#),Q).$$
Here Hom from a presheaf means presheaf morphisms. Each inverse is the corresponding reverse reindexing or the unique factorization. In particular the two extensions of $TP\to T(P^\#)$ and $TP\to(TP)^\#$ give maps $(TP)^\#\rightleftarrows T(P^\#)$ whose composites are identities by uniqueness. This gives a natural isomorphism $T(P^\#)\cong(TP)^\#$, compatible with the sheafification maps.

source.place: Tag 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules), universal property; elementary reindexing argument

proof.text:
For $P=\mathcal F\otimes_{p,\mathcal O}\mathcal G$, the definition [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] gives, naturally in $U$,
$$TP(U)=\mathcal F(\Phi U)\otimes_{\mathcal O(\Phi U)}\mathcal G(\Phi U)=(T\mathcal F\otimes_{p,R}T\mathcal G)(U).$$
The restriction maps are identical, since both send $s\otimes t$ to $s|\otimes t|$. Sheafify this identity and use step 2 to obtain $\sigma:T(\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal G)\xrightarrow{\sim}T\mathcal F\otimes_R T\mathcal G$. Compatibility with the sheafification maps gives $T(s\otimes t)\mapsto Ts\otimes Tt$. For later use, two maps out of this sheaf tensor are equal if they agree on the sectionwise pure tensors: precompose with the presheaf tensor to sheafification map, use that pure tensors generate each algebraic tensor product, then use uniqueness in the sheafification universal property. For the iterated criterion one can work locally: if $P\to P^\#$ is the sheafification map of an abelian presheaf, its sheafification is an isomorphism by the universal property (both sheafifications are $P^\#$ with the same unit). Applying [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-iso-locally-bijective] shows that every section of $P^\#$ locally comes from $P$, and that two presheaf sections with the same image become equal on a covering. This applies to module sheafification because [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] constructs its underlying abelian sheaf by abelian sheafification. Thus a section of a sheaf tensor is locally a finite sum of pure tensors. In a nested tensor, locally express its finitely many inner tensor sections as finite sums, refining the finitely many coverings, and expand by bilinearity. Every nested tensor section is consequently locally a finite sum of nested pure tensors, so agreement there implies agreement everywhere by the sheaf separation axiom.

proof.text:
For $U\in\mathcal C$, the functor $\Phi_U:\mathcal C/U\to\mathcal D/\Phi U$ sends $(V\to U)$ to $(\Phi V\to\Phi U)$. Its inverse sends $(W\to\Phi U)$ to $(\Psi W\to\Psi\Phi U\cong U)$; the unit and counit come from those of $\Phi,\Psi$. Coverings are the underlying coverings, by [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], so these reindexings also preserve sheaves. Reindexing an $\mathcal O|_{\Phi U}$-linear natural transformation along $\Phi_U$ has inverse reindexing along this quasi-inverse, and identifies its source and target with $(T\mathcal F)|_U,(T\mathcal G)|_U$. Hence [def-pur-sheaf-hom] gives a bijective $R(U)$-linear map
$$T\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)(U)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O|_{\Phi U}}(\mathcal F|_{\Phi U},\mathcal G|_{\Phi U})\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{R|_U}((T\mathcal F)|_U,(T\mathcal G)|_U).$$
Explicitly, the component of the image of $\varphi$ at $(V\to U)$ is $\varphi_{\Phi V}$. For $U'\to U$, both restricting this map and first restricting $\varphi$ have that same component at every $V\to U'$. The bijections therefore define the sheaf isomorphism $\eta$, with the required local-section rule. No finite-presentation hypothesis is used.

proof.text: The constructions are natural in both variables. For module maps $a:\mathcal F\to\mathcal F'$ and $b:\mathcal G\to\mathcal G'$, both tensor-comparison composites send the sectionwise pure tensor $s\otimes t$ to $T a(s)\otimes T b(t)$, so they agree by the uniqueness criterion in step 3. For $a:\mathcal F'\to\mathcal F$ and $b:\mathcal G\to\mathcal G'$, the Hom-comparison square commutes because on every slice component reindexing sends $b\varphi a$ to $(Tb)(T\varphi)(Ta)$. These formulas are exactly covariant tensor naturality and contravariant/covariant Hom naturality.

proof.text: The associativity comparison commutes: starting with $T((s\otimes t)\otimes h)$, each path ends at $Ts\otimes(Tt\otimes Th)$. The symmetry comparison commutes because both paths send $T(s\otimes t)$ to $Tt\otimes Ts$. The left unit comparison commutes because both paths send $T(a\otimes s)$ to $Ta\,Ts=T(as)$. The right unit comparison commutes because both paths send $T(s\otimes a)$ to $Ta\,Ts=T(as)$. Equality on these tensors implies equality of the sheaf maps by the iterated uniqueness criterion in step 3. Here the standard associator, symmetry and unit maps are defined by the formulas $(s\otimes t)\otimes h\mapsto s\otimes(t\otimes h)$, $s\otimes t\mapsto t\otimes s$, $a\otimes s\mapsto as$, and $s\otimes a\mapsto as$. For the associator, locally represent an inner section $w$ as $\sum_i s_i\otimes t_i$ using step 3 and send $w\otimes h$ to $\sum_i s_i\otimes(t_i\otimes h)$. The algebraic tensor relations show that this is independent of a presheaf tensor representation; if two representations have equal images in the inner sheaf tensor, step 3 makes them equal as presheaf tensors on a further covering, so their proposed images agree there. Separation makes the images agree on overlaps and the sheaf axiom glues them. The resulting map is bilinear, hence extends from the outer presheaf tensor by the sheafification universal property. To construct the inverse, locally represent a section $v$ of $\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal H$ by $\sum_j t_j\otimes h_j$ and send $s\otimes v$ to $\sum_j(s\otimes t_j)\otimes h_j$. Tensor relations make this independent of the presheaf representation; local injectivity from step 3 makes two lifts agree after refinement, so separation and gluing give a well-defined bilinear map on sheaves. The sheafification universal property extends it over the outer tensor. The two composites fix $(s\otimes t)\otimes h$ and $s\otimes(t\otimes h)$, respectively, so step 3 proves that they are identities. The flip is its own inverse; the left and right unit inverses are respectively $s\mapsto1\otimes s$ and $s\mapsto s\otimes1$. Their formulas respect the tensor relations and restrictions, and so extend by sheafification. This constructs the maps used in the verification above from step 3 and the definitions. For powers use the recursion of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]: the $m=1$ comparison is the identity; the $(m+1)$ comparison is $\sigma_{\mathcal F^{\otimes m},\mathcal F}$ followed by the tensor product of the $m$ comparison and the identity. Induction gives an isomorphism for every $m\geq1$, and the associativity verification ensures compatibility with rebracketing.

proof.text: Given $\alpha:\mathcal O\to\mathcal O'$, regard $\mathcal O'$ as an $\mathcal O$-module through $\alpha$. Substitute $\mathcal G=\mathcal O'$ in step 3. The reindexed action is through $T\alpha:R\to T\mathcal O'$, so the result is precisely $g^{-1}(\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal O')\cong g^{-1}\mathcal F\otimes_{g^{-1}\mathcal O}g^{-1}\mathcal O'$, with change of rings as in [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. This proves the claimed $R$-linear isomorphism for any ring sheaf $\mathcal O'$. When $\mathcal O'$ is commutative, it also respects the $T\mathcal O'$-actions: multiplication by a local section $b$ sends $s\otimes t$ to $s\otimes bt$ on both sides, and the equality extends by step 3. This extra linearity uses commutativity to commute $b$ with the image of $\alpha$ in the tensor balancing relation. No flatness of $\mathcal O'$ is required.

Finally [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit] computes module inverse limits sectionwise. For every $U$, under step 1 the canonical comparison is the identity identification
$$T(\varprojlim_n\mathcal F_n)(U)=(\varprojlim_n\mathcal F_n)(\Phi U)=\{(x_n):t_n(x_{n+1})=x_n\}=\varprojlim_n(T\mathcal F_n)(U).$$
Both restrictions and the $R(U)=\mathcal O(\Phi U)$-action are componentwise, so the identifications give an $R$-linear sheaf isomorphism. Its composites with every projection are the reindexed projections, showing that it is the canonical map in the statement, naturally in the inverse system.
